issue.title: [8.x] Return Default User::class FQCN if no model key is defined in config
issue.body: As issued in #40345 this is a first idea to solve this Problem by return the default value of model Key in auth.php['providers']['users']['model'] using database instead of eloquent.

body: You're changing the guard to one that doesn't have a model. Then it's normal that you'll get an error. A policy always requires a model.

@driesvints the command is generating invalid code. The problem is that **I am not getting an error**. The fact that I have a custom user provider is not documented anywhere as related to this, and even if it were, spitting out an error or warning or an explanatory message all seem more appropriate than generating a half-stub that is really hard to decode.
@slavicd ah I see what you mean. What would need to happen here is that the `if (! $model) {` throws an exception I think instead of the stub. Because a model is clearly required here.
Precisely. I'll try to write a PR now.

issue.title: [8.x] Throws an error upon make:policy if no model class is configured
issue.body:
If the model config key is not present in `auth.providers.users` the `make:policy` command will silently spit out some very poor stub.

Fixes: #40345
